stories.title: US stocks rise, dollar slides as investors digest Democrats’ midterm victories
summary: Government bond yields fall while initial fears ease over impact of election results on world’s biggest economyUS midterm elections – live updatesAfter US midterms, what will lame-duck Trump mean for global economy?US stocks have surged as investors digest the Democrats’ victories in the midterm elections, lifted by hopes that Donald Trump’s turbulent policymaking would be restrained and shaking off initial fears about the impact on growth in the world’s largest economy.The Dow Jones rose close to 3%, its best day in over a year, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq and the benchmark S&P 500 gained about 1.5% each when markets closed on Wednesday afternoon, turning around overnight falls in US stock futures after the news that the Democratic party won control of the Senate and the House of Representatives.

stories.title: CVS Health to split pharmacy chain from health insurance
summary: CVS Pharmacy will be separate from CVS Health, housing major insurer Aetna and benefits manager CaremarkCVS Health, the largest US healthcare conglomerate valued at $117bn, has announced its plans split off its pharmacy chain from its health insurance and benefits businesses, ending an era in which healthcare companies grew into vast conglomerates.In their announcement on Wednesday, CVS Health said they will split off its 9,000 pharmacies, in-store clinics and mail order prescription business into a business named CVS Pharmacy.

stories.title: Trump blamed Fox News for Republican losses even as network’s hosts went easy on him
summary: Fox News pundits hardly criticized the US president in midterms coverage but Trump was still quick to cast blameUS midterms 2026 live – latest updatesTrack live results from all 50 statesTell us: what do you want to know about the midterm election results?In the weeks leading up to Tuesday’s midterm elections, Donald Trump made clear that he would place some blame on his favorite cable channel, Fox News, if his party did poorly.On election day, he didn’t disappoint.This article was amended on 4 November 2026; a previous version incorrectly stated that Karoline Leavitt is Donald Trump’s most recent press secretary, when it is in fact Katie Zacharia.
